records.status: established by enumeration of project files and ontology cross-references (descriptive, not a hypothesis test)
records.label: Proxy-fish gene records reach 14 of the flying-fish blueprint's 257 cell types, and the cause is the ontology crosswalk, not the data: only 16 of the 257 cell types have any zebrafish-anatomy equivalent to map through

records.status: established by enumeration of ZFIN and Bgee records (descriptive)
records.label: In proxy fish, 982 genes are expressed in the pectoral fin, 166 are required for it (a loss-of-function phenotype under standard conditions) and 1 verified gain-of-function gene, kcnk5b, is sufficient to enlarge it

records.status: supported (by the cited abstracts, each quoted verbatim; no new experiment)
records.label: Three published findings connect potassium channels to fin size in zebrafish and to fin proportion in flying fishes, and each was verified against its PubMed abstract: kcnk5b gain of function enlarges fins, longfin overexpresses kcnh2a, and Daane 2021 implicates lat4a with kcnh2a in flying-fish fin proportion

records.status: serendipitous methodological finding, established by enumeration
records.label: Bgee 15.2 and ZFIN's Ensembl 1:1 table use different Ensembl releases, so 1614 zebrafish genes (fgf10a and shha among them) appeared twice under different ids until merged on exact symbol

records.status: serendipitous methodological finding, established by enumeration
records.label: ZFIN's "clean" phenotype file carries no experimental condition and is almost entirely standard conditions; 1034 attached abnormal rows whose annotation ZFIN also recorded under a treatment experiment, or that were uniquely non-standard, were dropped from "required for", and 2095 more came from dominant alleles without a truncating consequence, where loss of function is not established

records.status: documented refusal (observed at the stated time)
records.label: The Bgee SPARQL endpoint refused the thread's query with HTTP 403 (a Cloudflare challenge page), so expression came from Bgee's bulk call files instead

records.status: supported (published measurements, re-tabulated; no new measurement)
records.label: Measured on 49 museum flying-fish specimens (3 species, standard length 1.68 to 24 cm), pectoral fin length is 0.406 to 0.823 of standard length (median 0.687), against 0.14 in halfbeaks and 0.088 in needlefishes (Daane et al. 2021, Data S1A)

records.status: serendipitous methodological finding, reproduced with two logged probe queries
records.label: Ubergraph stores ontology cross-reference values as xsd:string-typed literals, so a SPARQL VALUES block of plain literals matches nothing and returns an empty result with HTTP 200: the same query for the pectoral fin's ZFA cross-reference returned 0 rows with a plain literal and 1 row with a typed literal

records.status: mixed within one reading: the chain is supported end to end at sufficiency, while the direction of its bioelectric step is inconclusive (see genotype/nanopubs/DECISIONS.md for why this is one record and not two)
records.label: The best-supported gene-to-phenotype chain for fin size runs from the potassium channel kcnk5b to increased zebrafish fin length, but its middle link is contradicted: three papers disagree on whether the growth-driving membrane-potential change is a hyperpolarization or a depolarization, and no recording has ever been made from a fin cell

records.status: supported, at the weakest useful grade (association): a morphological comparison, not a manipulation in a flying fish
records.label: The one flying-fish trait that can be compared with the two zebrafish fin-overgrowth mutants argues against kcnk5b as the flying-fish mechanism: flying fishes and the longfin (kcnh2a) mutant keep regular fin-ray segmentation, whereas the kcnk5b mutant has irregular segmentation

The flying-fish candidate gene lat4a (ZFIN slc43a2a) has the weakest causal chain of the three fin-size genes: nothing experimental connects its amino-acid transport function to fin ray length, so that link is graded hypothesis, and every fin phenotype for the gene comes from a single publication

records.status: serendipitous methodological finding, established by inspection of the ZFIN files and the cited papers
records.label: ZFIN holds zero phenotype rows for kcnh2a because the longfin phenotypes are filed against the chromosomal feature rather than against the gene, so a gene-keyed pipeline silently misses the best-known fin-overgrowth mutant; and the clone-autonomy experiment behind its sufficiency grade used human KCNH2, not the zebrafish gene
